name: Seychelles
summary: 115 islands in the Indian Ocean, uninhabited until French settlers and enslaved Africans arrived in 1770; British from 1814 and independent in 1976.

location.value: Indian Ocean north-east of Madagascar; about 455 km².

terrain.value: Granite islands with steep green hills, such as Mahé, Praslin and La Digue, and flat outer coral islands and atolls such as Aldabra.

climate.value: Tropical and warm all year, with a north-west monsoon (December–March) and a south-east trade-wind season (May–October).

resources.value: Beaches and coral reefs for tourism, rich tuna fishing grounds, and coconuts and cinnamon.

disasters.value: The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami damaged coasts; rising seas and coastal erosion threaten the low islands.

urbanisation.value: Most people live in and around the capital.

disease.value: Good basic health care; rising diabetes.

migration.value: Some Seychellois emigrate for work and study, mainly to Britain and Australia; foreign workers come for tourism and building.

economicBase.value: Tourism and fishing, especially tuna caught by foreign fleets and canned at Port Victoria, plus offshore finance.

tradeRoutes.value: Port Victoria, one of the busiest tuna ports in the Indian Ocean, and the international airport on Mahé (1971).

wealth.value: A high-income economy and one of Africa’s richest countries per person, though some families remain poor.

moneyAndTax.value: The Seychellois rupee; after a debt default in 2008 the country floated the rupee and reformed taxes.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A presidential republic: the elected president is head of state and government, with a National Assembly.

keyRulers.value: James Mancham, first president (1976–77), and France-Albert René, who took power in a 1977 coup and ruled until 2004.

succession.value: Multi-party elections since 1993; in 2020 an opposition candidate won the presidency for the first time.

institutions.value: The National Assembly, an elected presidency and the courts, under the 1993 constitution.

stability.value: A coup in 1977 led to one-party rule until 1993; since then politics has been peaceful.

eliteConflict.value: Rivalry between the long-ruling party founded by René and the opposition, which won elections in 2016 and 2020.

armyAndTech.value: The small Seychelles Defence Forces and Coast Guard patrol a huge sea area against piracy and illegal fishing.

majorWars.value: No wars since independence; a mercenary coup attempt failed in 1981 and Somali piracy was a threat around 2009–12.

territoryChange.value: In 1976 Britain returned the islands of Aldabra, Farquhar and Desroches, which it had separated in 1965.

alliancesRivals.value: A member of the Commonwealth, African Union, SADC and Indian Ocean Commission; close ties to India, the UAE and the EU.

inventions.value: No major inventions; the country is known for marine conservation and protecting rare species such as the coco de mer.

scienceEducation.value: Free schooling and high literacy; the University of Seychelles opened in 2009.

openness.value: Very open to tourism and foreign investment, and visitors from most countries need no visa.

communicationTransport.value: Ferries and short flights link Mahé, Praslin and La Digue; Air Seychelles flies to other countries.

religion.value: About three-quarters Roman Catholic, with Anglican, other Christian, Hindu and Muslim minorities.

languageWriting.value: Seychellois Creole (Kreol), based on French, is the national language; English and French are also official.

artsArchitecture.value: Wooden Creole plantation houses with verandas, and moutya and sega music and dance.

socialStructure.value: Mixed African, European and Asian descent.

sharedIdentity.value: A Creole island identity mixing African, French, British and Asian influences, shared through the Kreol language.

dailyLife.value: Fish curries with rice, breadfruit and fresh fruit; many people work in hotels, fishing or government.

neighbours.value: Islands of the western Indian Ocean: Madagascar, Mauritius, Comoros and the Maldives; Kenya and Tanzania to the west.

ideasReligions.value: Catholic Christianity, a revival of Kreol language and culture since the 1980s, and strong conservation ideas.

riseSignals.value: Became independent from Britain on 29 June 1976 as a republic in the Commonwealth.

peakPeriod.value: Too recent to judge; growth from tourism has made it one of the richest countries in Africa.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Still in existence as the Republic of Seychelles, a small island state with an economy built on tourism.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
